newsitem.title: ITALY: RUGBY UNION-IRFB INTRODUCES USE OF SUBSTITUTES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRFB INTRODUCES USE OF SUBSTITUTES.

text.p: Rugby union on Thursday followed the lead of rugby league and soccer by introducing the use of tactical substitutions.
The International Rugby Football Board (IRFB) said it had sanctioned the use of five substitutes, two of whom can only be for front row players, at any time during a match.
Previously only four replacements were allowed to cover for injured players. Now up to six replacements may be used in the case of injury, five of whom can double as substitutes.
"By allowing substitutes, an opportunity is being provided to enhance team performance," IRFB chairman Vernon Pugh said in a statement at the end of a three-day council meeting in Rome.
"We also believe this decision makes the game more honest in that it addresses concerns about players feigning injuries."
The changes, which will operate in international and senior club matches, take effect from November 4.
In safety-related changes, the IRFB ruled that it would no longer be possible to add players to a scrum and line-out jumpers should not be supported below the waist.
Pugh said the new line-out rule was introduced to counter the risk of injury, especially among younger and less experienced players.

The IRFB also introduced in-goal judges for seven-a-side rugby and, in a move to improve the tempo of the game, ruled that the kick-off after a score should be taken by the scoring team -- giving the defending side an opportunity to regain possession.
